chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Our muscle cells perform ____ type of respiration during exercise.
solution: **(B)** Anaerobic. During exercise the muscle cells need energy faster than oxygen can be supplied to them, so they break down glucose without oxygen. Glucose is incompletely oxidised, less energy is produced and lactic acid accumulates in the muscles, due to which we feel tired. Fermentation is only one step of anaerobic respiration and the Krebs cycle is a step of aerobic respiration, so neither names the type of respiration.

stem: Which of the following animals can regenerate its broken body part?
solution: **(D)** Starfish. The starfish belongs to phylum Echinodermata, whose animals have a good ability of regeneration. In certain situations a starfish can break apart its body parts and regenerate them later on.

stem: Government of India has encouraged the ____ for improving the productivity by launching NKM-16.
solution: **(C)** Pisciculture. NKM-16 is the Nil-Kranti Mission-2016 (Blue Revolution). Through it the Government of India encourages people to take up pisciculture (fish farming) to increase the production of fishes and other aquatic organisms, and offers 50% to 100% subsidies for it.

stem: At the district level ____ is responsible for disaster management and implementation of rehabilitation schemes.
solution: **(A)** Collector. The District Collector is the chairman of the District Disaster Management Authority. He plans, coordinates and controls disaster management in the district and is responsible for implementing the rehabilitation schemes. The Tahsildar works at the taluka level.

stem: ____ of West Bengal is reserved for tigers.
solution: **(D)** Sundarban National Park. The Sundarban National Park of West Bengal is reserved for tigers; its tiger population is now threatened by dams, deforestation and excessive fishing. Manas National Park and Molai Jungle are in Assam, and the Western Ghat is a biodiversity hotspot, not a park of West Bengal.

stem: State whether the following statement is True or False: Evolution is the gradual change occurring in living organisms over a long duration.
solution: True. Evolution is the gradual change occurring in living organisms over a long duration. Through such slow changes, simple organisms gave rise to more complex organisms over millions of years.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Write the name of any one sexual disease.
solution: Syphilis is a sexual disease. (Gonorrhoea is another sexual disease that occurs on a large scale.)

stem: Select odd man out: Gutkha, Yoga, Alcoholic drinks, Cigarette.
solution: Yoga is the odd man out. Gutkha, alcoholic drinks and cigarettes are addictive substances that harm health, whereas yoga is a healthy practice that keeps the body fit and helps to relieve stress.

stem: Fill in the box with proper word: Kinetic Energy in wind \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) Electric energy
solution: Kinetic Energy in wind \(\rightarrow\) **Kinetic energy in turbine** \(\rightarrow\) Electric energy. The wind strikes the blades of the wind turbine and rotates them, and the rotating turbine drives the generator, which produces electric energy.

stem: Match the correct pair: Column A: Xylitol. Column B: (a) To impart acidity (b) To impart sweetness (c) Pigment.
solution: Xylitol : (b) To impart sweetness. Xylitol is obtained by microbial processing and is used as a low-calorie artificial sweetener in food materials.

stem: Give scientific reason: Some of the organs in human body are most valuable.
solution: Organs of the human body may become less efficient or completely functionless due to aging, accidents, infections or disorders, and the life of such a person becomes difficult or may even end. If the person gets a healthy organ by transplantation, the life can be saved. Organs like the liver, heart and eyes can be donated only after death, and a person can donate one of the pair of kidneys during life. Since a donated organ can save a life or give vision to the blind, and such donors are hard to find, some of the organs in the human body are most valuable.

stem: Give scientific reason: Hydroelectric energy, solar energy and wind energy are called renewable energies.
solution: Hydroelectric energy, solar energy and wind energy are obtained from water stored in reservoirs, sunlight and wind. These sources are never-ending (perpetual): the water in a reservoir is replenished every rainy season, and sunlight and wind are available again and again in nature. Since these sources do not get exhausted on use, unlike coal or natural gas, the energies obtained from them are called renewable energies.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Give scientific reason: Fibres are one of the important nutrients.
solution: We cannot digest fibres, so they do not give us energy. However, fibres help in the digestion of other food substances and in the egestion (removal) of undigested substances from the body. Hence fibres, obtained from leafy vegetables, fruits and cereals, are one of the important nutrients.

stem: Observe the given animals (Fig. A and Fig. B) and answer the questions: (a) Identify the animals shown in above figure. (b) State the type of evidence of evolution related to above animals.
solution:
(a) Fig. A is the duck-billed platypus and Fig. B is the lungfish.

(b) These animals are connecting links, which are evidence of evolution. A connecting link shows characters of two different groups. The duck-billed platypus lays eggs like reptiles but has mammary glands and hair like mammals. The lungfish is a fish but respires with lungs like amphibians. These examples indicate that mammals evolved from reptiles and amphibians evolved from fishes.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Fill in the box with proper word: Asexual reproduction in multicellular organisms \(\rightarrow\) ____ and ____ (two boxes).
solution:
Asexual reproduction in multicellular organisms \(\rightarrow\) **Fragmentation** and **Regeneration**.

In fragmentation the body of the organism breaks into pieces and each piece grows into a new organism (e.g. Spirogyra). In regeneration a part of the body grows into a complete new organism (e.g. Planaria). Budding, vegetative propagation and spore formation are the other methods of asexual reproduction in multicellular organisms.

stem: Give two examples of each: (a) Physical problems arising due to excessive use of mobile phones. (b) Activities under the jurisdiction of cyber crime laws.
solution:
(a) Physical problems due to excessive use of mobile phones: (1) headache and tiredness, (2) insomnia (lack of sleep). Problems in vision, forgetfulness, tinnitus and joint pains may also arise.

(b) Activities under the jurisdiction of cyber crime laws: (1) hacking, that is obtaining confidential information of the government, institutes or companies from the internet and misusing it, (2) piracy, that is the illegal use or sale of others' software, music, videos or literature obtained from the internet. Opening a fake Facebook account to tease or cheat others is also a cyber crime.

stem: Write any two objectives of disaster management.
solution: Two objectives of disaster management: (1) Saving human life during the calamity and releasing the people trapped in it. (2) Supplying essential commodities to the people to reduce the effect of the disaster. Rehabilitating the disaster victims and taking protective measures so that the disaster does not recur, or its intensity is reduced, are further objectives.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Distinguish between Sexual reproduction and Asexual reproduction.
solution:
| Sexual reproduction | Asexual reproduction |
|---|---|
| Two parents (a male and a female) are generally involved. | Only one parent is involved (uniparental). |
| Male and female gametes are formed and they fuse (fertilisation). | Gametes are not formed and there is no fertilisation. |
| Gametes are formed by meiosis. | It occurs by mitotic cell division. |
| Genetic recombination occurs, so the offspring show variations. | No genetic recombination occurs, so the offspring are genetically identical to the parent. |
| It is a comparatively slow process. | It is a fast process. |
| Example: human beings, flowering plants. | Example: binary fission in Amoeba, budding in Hydra. |

stem: Complete the chart: Lipids \(\rightarrow\) a; Carbohydrates \(\rightarrow\) Glycolysis \(\rightarrow\) c \(\rightarrow\) d; Proteins \(\rightarrow\) b; a and b also lead into d; d \(\rightarrow\) e \(\rightarrow\) f. Fill in the boxes a to f.
solution:
| Box | Answer |
|---|---|
| a | Fatty acids |
| b | Amino acids |
| c | Pyruvic acid |
| d | Acetyl-CoA |
| e | Krebs cycle |
| f | \(CO_2 + H_2O\) + Energy |

Carbohydrates are broken down by glycolysis into pyruvic acid, which is converted into acetyl-CoA. When carbohydrates are insufficient, lipids are converted into fatty acids and proteins into amino acids, and these too are converted into acetyl-CoA. Acetyl-CoA is completely oxidised in the Krebs cycle in the mitochondria, releasing \(CO_2\), \(H_2O\) and energy.

stem: Answer the following questions: (a) Define vestigial organs. (b) Write names of any two vestigial organs in human body. (c) Write the names of any two vestigial organs which are non-functional in human beings but functional in other organisms.
solution:
(a) Degenerated or underdeveloped useless organs of organisms are called vestigial organs.

(b) Two vestigial organs in the human body: the tail-bone (coccyx) and the wisdom teeth. Body hair, the appendix and the muscles of the ear pinna are also vestigial in humans.

(c) (1) The appendix: useless in human beings but a fully functional organ in ruminants. (2) The muscles of the ear pinna: useless in human beings but useful in monkeys for moving the ear pinna.

stem: Complete the following flow chart: (a) Generation of electrical energy using thermal energy: Fuel Coal \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) Generator \(\rightarrow\) Electrical energy, with a ____ box below that takes from the second blank and returns to the first. (b) Energy transformation in thermal power plant: Chemical energy in coal \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) Electrical energy.
solution:
(a) Fuel Coal \(\rightarrow\) **Boiler for conversion of water to steam** \(\rightarrow\) **Steam turbine** \(\rightarrow\) Generator \(\rightarrow\) Electrical energy. Lower box: **System for converting steam back to water** (condenser). The steam leaving the turbine goes to this system, is condensed back to water, and the water is re-circulated to the boiler.

(b) Chemical energy in coal \(\rightarrow\) **Thermal energy** \(\rightarrow\) **Kinetic energy in steam** \(\rightarrow\) **Kinetic energy in turbine** \(\rightarrow\) Electrical energy.
figureNote: Two flow charts on p-06: (a) Fuel Coal, two blank boxes, Generator, Electrical energy, with a long blank box below receiving an arrow from the second blank and sending an arrow up to the first; (b) Chemical energy in coal, three blank boxes, Electrical energy

stem:
Complete the paragraph with the help of words given in the bracket: (Lactobacillus cremoris, Protease, Cow, Vegetarian, microbiological, rennet, Geobacter, Saccharomyces)

Cheese is produced on large scale from the abundantly available ____ milk all over the world. First chemical and ____ tests of milk are performed. Some colours and microbes like Lactobacillus lactis, ____ and Streptococcus thermophilus are mixed with milk. It imparts sourness to the milk. After this, to impart the dense texture, whey needs to be removed. An enzyme ____ obtained from alimentary canal of cattle was being traditionally used earlier. However an enzyme ____ obtained from fungi is used at present to produce ____ cheese.
solution: Cheese is produced on large scale from the abundantly available **cow** milk all over the world. First chemical and **microbiological** tests of milk are performed. Some colours and microbes like *Lactobacillus lactis*, **Lactobacillus cremoris** and *Streptococcus thermophilus* are mixed with milk. It imparts sourness to the milk. After this, to impart the dense texture, whey needs to be removed. An enzyme **rennet** obtained from alimentary canal of cattle was being traditionally used earlier. However an enzyme **protease** obtained from fungi is used at present to produce **vegetarian** cheese.

stem: Write a short note on the importance of medicinal plants.
solution: India has been gifted with great biodiversity and has a great tradition of ayurveda, which cures diseases with the help of natural sources such as medicinal plants. Medicinal plants contain active ingredients that are used as medicines; for example, the leaves of Adulsa (*Adhatoda vasica*) contain vasicine, which is used against cough, and Neem (*Azadirachta indica*) is another important medicinal plant. Ayurvedic preparations like Balghuti are made from such plant components. Earlier, medicinal plants were collected from the forest, but due to the depletion of forest area they are becoming rare. Hence medicinal plants are now cultivated, which conserves them, supplies raw material for medicines and gives income to farmers.

stem: Explain the importance of good communication with others.
solution: Good communication with friends, peers, cousins, teachers and, more importantly, parents helps us to express our feelings to our near and dear ones, and this relieves mental stress. It helps us to establish harmonious relations with relatives and other members of society, so we do not become solitary or self-centred. When we communicate well, we become sensitive towards others, help them in need and get help when we need it. Thus good communication keeps our mental and social health sound.

stem: Identify the type of disaster and write its effect: (a) Terrorism (b) Forest fire (c) Theft.
solution:
| Disaster | Type | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Terrorism | Man-made disaster | Loss of human life and property, and fear and instability in the country. |
| (b) Forest fire | Natural disaster (biological, plant type) | Destruction of forests and wildlife, and air pollution that adversely affects the environment. |
| (c) Theft | Man-made disaster | Loss of money and property, and a feeling of insecurity and mental stress among people. |

stem: Complete the following flow chart explaining my role in environmental conservation: My Role in Environmental Conservation \(\rightarrow\) Conservation, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____ (six boxes, one filled).
solution:

stem: Observe the following picture (Fig. A and Fig. B). Write the answers of the following questions: (a) Identify the class of animals shown in above picture. (b) Which similarities are shown in above animals from the adaptation point of view? (c) Why these animals are included in different classes inspite of their similarities?
solution:
(a) Fig. A is a shark (dog fish), which belongs to class Pisces. Fig. B is a pigeon, which belongs to class Aves.

(b) Similarities from the adaptation point of view: (1) Both have a spindle-shaped (streamlined) body; in the fish it minimises water resistance during swimming and in the bird it minimises air resistance during flight. (2) Both have paired organs of locomotion suited to their medium: fins in the fish and wings (modified forelimbs) in the bird. (3) In both, the tail helps to steer the body during movement.

(c) These similarities are only adaptations for moving through water and air. Animals are classified on their basic characters, and these differ. Pisces are cold-blooded aquatic animals with scales, fins and gills for respiration. Aves are warm-blooded animals with feathers as exoskeleton, forelimbs modified into wings, jaws modified into a beak and lungs for respiration. Hence, in spite of their similarities, the shark and the pigeon are included in different classes.
